topic: Roger Shepard & Jacqueline Metzler (1971) 10-Cube 3D Mental Rotation, Linear 60-Degrees-Per-Second Slope, and Parietal-Premotor Simulation (Low-Poly Pastel v7)
act5_climax_episode: Neuroimaging and spatial training proving parietal and premotor hand circuits physically simulate 3D block rotation.

clips.attire_and_hands: tweed jacket sleeves and cool porcelain-white gloved low-poly hands over a cool slate-stone bench
clips.prop_action: cool porcelain-white gloved low-poly hands lift and set two cool mist-white ten-cube L-shaped sculptures onto brushed-silver pedestals
clips.consequence: the two asymmetric ten-cube sculptures rest angled apart in crisp daylight

clips.environment: a sunlit cool mist-white Stanford psychology laboratory with a twin-circle display hood, response levers, and cool slate-stone desks
clips.action: viewed strictly from behind, a clothed low-poly volunteer in a sage-green sweater sits before the twin-circle screen and rests hands on silver levers

clips.attire_and_hands: tailored blazer cuffs and cool porcelain-white gloved low-poly hands at a brushed-silver turntable stand
clips.prop_action: cool porcelain-white gloved low-poly hands grip and rotate the right cool mist-white ten-cube sculpture smoothly through steady degree ticks
clips.consequence: a brushed-silver timer needle sweeps steadily as the ten-cube elbow aligns

clips.environment: the bright Stanford cognitive lab with two clothed low-poly researchers beside a tall brushed-silver diagonal step-bar stand
clips.action: viewed strictly from behind, two clothed low-poly scientists in slate-blue blazers step beside the console and align a ten-cube model with the twin-circle screen

clips.structure: a clean architectural side cutaway of the cool mist-white viewing console linking the twin-circle block screen, twin silver levers, and rising step-bar rack
